intended_object: The standard diagonal maximal torus embedding of the rank-m split torus into Sp₂ₘ on A-valued points, t = (t₀,…,tₘ₋₁) ↦ diag(t₀,…,tₘ₋₁, t₀⁻¹,…,tₘ₋₁⁻¹). Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition is a chain of four maps. First, an A-point of the split torus (an R-algebra map from the Laurent group algebra R[ℤ^m] to A) is turned into a family of units `Fin m → Aˣ`, using `SplitTorus.pointsMulEquiv` followed by `diagonalTorusCoordinates`, which only strips the `ULift`. Second, `GLSymplecticFin.diagonal` builds the diagonal matrix from `diagonalCoordinates`, which is `t i` on the first block and `(t i)⁻¹` on the second. Finally, the matrix is turned back into an A-point of the coordinate Hopf algebra of Sp₂ₘ via the inverse of `pointsMulEquiv`.

The result is the standard map t ↦ diag(t, t⁻¹) into the symplectic group, written in the block coordinates Fin (m+m). The same file proves that the map is a homomorphism, injective, natural in A, and satisfies the pinning equations for the root subgroups. This matches the textbook diagonal torus of type C (Milne §23, Humphreys §26.3).

The generality is natural: any commutative base ring R and any commutative R-algebra A. Since this is a specific object, the fixed rank m and the Fin-indexed coordinates are not a narrowing. Mathlib has no symplectic group scheme or diagonal-torus morphism to compare with.
